facts.claim: Ballarat is a city about 110 km north-west of Melbourne in the Goldfields region, with about 117,000 people, the third largest city in Victoria.
Gold was discovered at Poverty Point on 18 August 1851, turning a sheep station into a major settlement within months.
The Battle of Eureka Stockade, the only armed rebellion in Australian history, took place on 3 December 1854; the Eureka Flag is held in Ballarat.
Sovereign Hill is a 25-hectare open-air museum depicting Ballarat's first ten years after the 1851 gold discovery, one of Victoria's most popular attractions.

Ballarat Botanical Gardens were established in 1857 and hold the greatest concentration of public statuary, including the Prime Ministers Avenue; Lake Wendouree hosted the 1956 Olympic rowing and kayaking.
Ballarat Tramway Museum runs historic trams on 1.3 km of original track beside Lake Wendouree on weekends and holidays.

experiences: Stroll the botanical gardens and lake

tips.title: Trams run weekends only
tips.detail: The Ballarat Tramway Museum's trams run on weekends, public and school holidays, from the afternoon (12:30-5pm).

tips.title: Easy day trip from Melbourne
tips.detail: Ballarat is about 110 km north-west of Melbourne, with train and car routes; the town's big sights are spread out, so plan transport.

tips.title: Begonia Festival in March
tips.detail: The Begonia Festival, over the Labour Day long weekend in March, fills Lake Wendouree and Sturt St, so book ahead.

best_months.rationale: Inferred: Wikipedia gives Ballarat a mean max of 17.4C at 435-630 m elevation, so cooler than Melbourne; the Begonia Festival is in March. No source states best months, unverified.

seasonal_tags: Begonia Festival (March, Labour Day weekend) is a real annual pattern; optional.

facts.claim: Geelong is a port city on Corio Bay about 75 km south-west of Melbourne, and Victoria's second-largest city with 282,809 people in 2023.
It is the gateway to the Bellarine Peninsula and the Great Ocean Road.
The Geelong Waterfront is a working maritime area with cafes, an antique carousel and botanical gardens.
The National Wool Museum on Moorabool St takes about 90 minutes and includes a tourist information office.
You Yangs Regional Park, 22 km north of Geelong, has four main walks including a 3.2 km walk to Flinders Peak (348 m) with expansive views.
The 35 km Bellarine Rail Trail starts near South Geelong Station and runs to Queenscliff.

experiences: Climb for views at the You Yangs

tips.title: Avalon Airport is close
tips.detail: Avalon Airport, a second Melbourne-area airport, is about 20 minutes by road from Geelong, with a shuttle to Geelong and South Geelong stations.

tips.title: Cycle to Queenscliff
tips.detail: The Bellarine Rail Trail starts near South Geelong Station and runs 35 km to Queenscliff.

best_months.rationale: Wikivoyage says holidaymakers flock to Geelong's beaches on summer weekends; no source states best months, unverified.

facts.claim: Alpine National Park covers 6,474 km2 and is Victoria's largest national park, the Victorian continuation of Kosciuszko National Park.
It holds Victoria's highest point, Mount Bogong at 1,986 m, and the sub-alpine woodland and grassland of the Bogong High Plains.
Mount Feathertop (1,922 m) and Mount Hotham (1,862 m) are among its major peaks; Falls Creek and Mount Hotham are the ski resorts beside the park.
The 650 km Australian Alps Walking Track, from Walhalla to near Canberra, traverses the park.
The park protects threatened species including the spotted tree frog, she-oak skink, smoky mouse and mountain pygmy possum.
Paradise Falls is a 31 m fall reached via a viewing platform; best seen in spring or early summer.

experiences: Hike the Australian Alps Walking Track

tips.title: Winter means skis
tips.detail: In winter much of the park is snow-covered and only accessible on skis.

tips.title: No towns inside
tips.detail: There are no towns in the park; stay in Mount Hotham or Falls Creek, or the towns around it.

tips.title: Unsealed roads to falls
tips.detail: The road to Paradise Falls needs 11 km of unsealed driving; spring or early summer is the best time to see it.

best_months.rationale: Wikipedia: popular in summer for bushwalking and mountain biking, cooler alpine weather; winter snow-covered. Ski months Jun-Sep per seasonal tag (not sourced to dates).

seasonal_tags: Ski season at Falls Creek and Mount Hotham (winter, roughly June-September; months not sourced).

facts.claim: Echuca sits on the Murray River in Victoria, with the NSW border town of Moama opposite; population 15,056 (2021), 22,568 with Moama.
The port is home to the largest paddle steamer fleet in the world, including PS Adelaide (1866), the world's oldest operating wooden-hulled paddle steamer.
Historic vessels PS Pevensey (1911) and PS Alexander Arbuthnot (1923) operate commercially out of Echuca daily.
Echuca is about 2.5 hours' drive from Melbourne; trains take about 3 hours via Bendigo.
Annual events include the Southern 80 waterski race (February), described as the largest waterski race in the world.
Activities include riverboat cruises, watersports and eco tours; the Holden Motors museum is a listed sight.

experiences: Cruise the Murray on a paddle steamer

tips.title: Sit in the front carriages
tips.detail: On the train from Melbourne, sit in the front 3 cars; the rear 3 decouple at Bendigo.

tips.title: Easy to walk around
tips.detail: Apart from occasional buses there is no town transport, but the town is small enough to walk.

tips.title: Southern 80 in February
tips.detail: February brings the Southern 80 waterski race and a music festival, so expect busy river banks and book ahead.

best_months.rationale: Inferred; sources give no best-time guidance (Wikipedia: mean max 22.2C). Unverified.
